None of them contains a triangle, yet each needs one more color than the last." width="100%"} The Mycielski graphs are triangle-free graphs whose chromatic number grows by one at each step: `M(n)` has no three mutually joined nodes yet needs `n` colors. They are built by Mycielski's construction, starting from `M(1)`, a single node, and `M(2)`, a single edge. To go from `M(n-1)` to `M(n)`, add a "shadow" copy of each node joined to that node's neighbors, then one more node joined to every shadow. `M(3)` is the five-cycle and `M(4)` is the Grötzsch graph (11 nodes, 20 edges); the node count follows `3 * 2^(n-2) - 1`. Node numbering follows the construction: the nodes of `M(n-1)` first, then their shadows in the same order, then the extra node. In a directed graph every edge points from the earlier-created node to the later one. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Mycielski graphs are useful for: - showing that a graph can need many colors without containing a large clique - test cases for coloring heuristics and chromatic number bounds - examples of triangle-free graphs that are still fairly dense ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Index of the graph in the sequence, equal to its chromatic number. Must be at least `1`. Sizes roughly double at each step: `M(5)` has 23 nodes and `M(10)` has 767. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n=` is less than `1`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} `M(4)`, the Grötzsch graph, has `11` nodes and `20` edges: ::: {#8d4574ec .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_mycielski_graph(n=4) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (11, 20) ``` ::: ::: It contains no triangles, so its largest clique is a single edge, yet it needs four colors: ::: {#35563c7c .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} len(graph.list_triangles()), graph.clique_number() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (0, 2) ``` ::: :::
